title: How an Inkjet Printer Works in 60 Seconds 🖨️💧 #shorts
description:
A thermal inkjet printer fires ink with tiny bubbles. A resistor behind each nozzle heats the ink in microseconds, a vapor bubble shoves a droplet onto the paper, and when the bubble collapses fresh ink refills the chamber. Millions of cyan, magenta, yellow and black dots make the picture. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#inkjet #printer #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An inkjet print head heats ink at almost *a billion degrees* per second.

steps.label: Head
steps.text: The *print head* zips across the page, carrying rows of tiny *nozzles*.

steps.label: Heater
steps.text: Behind each nozzle sits a tiny *resistor* that flashes *hot* in microseconds.

steps.label: Bubble
steps.text: The ink boils into a *vapor bubble*, which shoves a *droplet* out of the nozzle.

steps.label: Refill
steps.text: The bubble *collapses*, and fresh ink flows in for the *next shot*.

steps.label: Dots
steps.text: Millions of *cyan, magenta, yellow* and *black* dots blend into your picture.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Heat, bubble, *droplet*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
